::: {#rem-one-or-all}
#### One example, or every element

Settling a quantified proposition takes one element in two cases,
and every element of the domain in the other two:

- To show that $\exists x \in S, P(x)$ is true,
  it is enough to find one $x$ in $S$ with $P(x)$ true.
- To show that $\forall x \in S, P(x)$ is false,
  it is enough to find one $x$ in $S$ with $P(x)$ false.
- To show that $\forall x \in S, P(x)$ is true,
  show $P(x)$ for every $x$ in $S$.
- To show that $\exists x \in S, P(x)$ is false,
  show that $P(x)$ is false for every $x$ in $S$.

When $S$ is infinite, the last two need a proof rather than a check of each element.

:::
